page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top. No marginal notes. Catchword "men" at the right below the last line, with the gathering signature at the left foot.

main_text.p: dam Olyntho Thraciæ proximū, con-iecti, egredi nequeunt, & sese distorquentes emoriūtur. Nos, etiam in medijs aduersis, cōtemplatione bonorū, quæ à Domino accepimus, & grata celebratione diuinæ beneficentiæ, nos ipsos exhilaremus, ac ærumnarum sensum minuamus: ac si quid in vita triste nobis evenit, haud secus obscuremus meliorum collatione, quàm solent Musici modulationibus aliis duriores obscurare harmonias.

Qui sibi, præter omne suum meritū, ab mimicis dictis cōtumeliosis & aperta vi, aut dolo malo, oppugnari videntur, in dulces amicos respicientes, nullos sibi inimicos esse vellent. Quasi vero, aut liberæ mimicor ū reprehensiones, siquidē eæ veræ sunt, non plurimū psint[?] homini nō φιλαυτία[?] excęcato, aut ex amicis non interdum fiant inimici? Recte profecto Nilus ille gnomographus dixit: Si quid mali de te dicit, verene, an falsò de te dicatur, perpende. S vere dictū animadverteris, vide ut emēdes: si non vere dictum vides, fumi euanescētis instar esse, cogitabis: sic ta-

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "psint[?]" (abbreviation with a stroke, possibly per-/pro-) and the Greek word "φιλαυτία[?]" (accent and final letters hard to make out). "emēdes" has a doubtful macron. The line "S vere" may be an abbreviated "Si". The running head is in spaced capitals. No page number is printed; the only foot mark is the signature.
